prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2017: Summary (≤500 words)

Core message
- Deliver a “real Brexit,” act as “guard dogs of Brexit,” and implement radical domestic reforms without raising taxes.

Brexit
- Six tests before exit is “complete”: full legal sovereignty outside EU courts; full control of immigration/borders; full maritime sovereignty and control of a 200‑mile EEZ; independent trade policy outside the Single Market and Customs Union; no divorce bill and retrieval of UK assets; completion by end‑2019.
- Prefer immediate repeal of the 1972 European Communities Act over Article 50; warn against EU “stalling.”
- Fisheries: leave Common Fisheries Policy; revoke 1964 London Convention; restore EEZ; end discards; license limited foreign access; land all UK‑caught fish in Britain; create Fisheries Protection Force.
- Reinstate blue UK passports in 2019.

Economy and tax
- Fund priorities with £35bn “savings”: cut foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrap HS2, reform Barnett Formula, end EU payments, departmental cuts; no tax rises.
- Cost of living: remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; scrap TV licence over 3 years; cut “green levies.”
- Tax: raise personal allowance to £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000 by 2022; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500k (aim to abolish); oppose probate hike.
- Crack down on multinational tax avoidance; prepare WTO‑terms trade if needed; promote “Buy British.”

Business and jobs
- Cut business rates 20% for premises <£50k RV; penalise chronic late payers; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for self‑employed.
- “British jobs for British workers”: require domestic advertising first; allow preference for under‑25 UK applicants; protect workers’ rights; curb zero‑hours abuse.
- Coastal Enterprise Zones: 50% business rate cut; regeneration, housing standards, and funding.

Housing
- Build up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes/year via a Housing Development Corporation on brownfield land; sold freehold to first‑time buyers under 40 with 10% deposit; resale back to HDC at cost+inflation; expand council housing; review housing associations.

Health and social care
- Extra £11bn/year for NHS and social care by 2021/22; integrate health and social care under a new department.
- Lift cap on medical school places; scrap tuition for doctors (NHS service tie‑in) and restore nursing/midwifery bursaries; more GPs, nurses, physician associates.
- Cut red tape; abolish PFI; manager licensing with accountability; scrap hospital parking fees; tighten overseas eligibility and pursue reciprocal charges.
- Mental health: +£500m/year; 28‑day max waits; school‑based counselling; integrate child–adult services; strong anti‑drug legal stance.

Education
- Grammar/technical school expansion (a grammar in every town); vocational “dual system”; restore maintenance grants; scrap tuition fees for STEM (service tie‑in) and for medicine (NHS tie‑in); better careers/employability education; preserve special schools.

Welfare, elderly, disability
- Maintain pension triple lock and universal pensioner benefits; +£2bn/year for social care; protect community services; improve carers’ support; reform disability assessments; end bedroom tax; protect disability benefits.

Immigration and integration
- Net migration to zero over five years via points‑based system and work permits; 5‑year moratorium on low‑skilled migration; seasonal schemes as needed.
- Visa rules: work (£30k+), student, visitor, family (restore “primary purpose” test); 5‑year NI/tax before welfare or non‑urgent NHS; private insurance requirement.
- Guarantee rights of pre‑Article 50 EU residents; tougher illegal immigration enforcement; deport foreign criminals.
- Integration: “one law for all”; plan to disband sharia councils; zero tolerance of FGM, forced marriage, “honour” crimes; ban face coverings in public; tough anti‑extremism measures in schools.

Law and order
- +20,000 police, +7,000 prison officers, +4,000 border staff; restore Stop and Search; keep prisons open; deport foreign prisoners; tackle drugs and prison extremism; repeal 2003 Licensing Act; opt out of European Arrest Warrant.

Defence and foreign policy
- Spend a genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus +£1bn/year; rebuild Army, Navy, RAF; overhaul procurement; retain nuclear deterrent; oppose EU defence integration.
- Veterans: new Veterans’ Administration, jobs guarantees, hostels, fast‑track healthcare; protect from historical legal pursuit.
- Foreign policy: “trade not aid,” reduce aid to 0.2% GNI, close DfID; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship; seek US FTA; cautious on interventions; engage Russia conditionally.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; invest in existing rail (esp. North); oppose Heathrow third runway; support regional airports; freeze and aim to scrap APD; expand EV charging; protect diesel drivers from punitive fees; support rural buses; foreign vehicle “Britdisc.”

Environment, farming, energy
- New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodlands; preference for brownfield; dredging to prevent floods; explore bottle deposit scheme.
- Agriculture: UK Single Farm Payment, capped at £120k; favour small/hill/organic farms; support antibiotic‑free livestock.
- Animal welfare: ban live exports; CCTV in abattoirs; clear slaughter labelling; tougher cruelty sentences.
- Energy: repeal Climate Change Act, leave Paris Agreement and EU ETS; diversify supply incl. shale gas (not in national parks); cut levies and unfair tariffs; review utilities’ profits.

Democracy and localism
- Abolish House of Lords; PR for Commons (reduced to 325 MPs); create an English Parliament; citizen‑initiated binding referenda; tighten postal voting; local binding referenda on major developments; keep council tax low.
